Maurice Ravel - Noctuelles; Oiseaux tristes (from Miroirs) Olivier Messiaen - Le Loriot (from Catalogue d'oiseaux) Michael Spencer - Ravelations (UnRavelling) Niki Zohdi - New Work [world premiere] Michael Finnissy - Third Political Agenda Michael Finnissy - Midsummer Morn (from English Country Tunes) Rolf Hind - Pakshina/Vrka/Matsya/Shatpadi/Khaga (Bird/Wolf/Fish/Bee/Bird) from Bhutani Alejandra Garcés - "Beauty is action, not contemplation." (I see the Pavilion and I see myself. As long as it exists intact and eternal, I can never truly exist. I have to destroy it so that the world can move again...) [world premiere] Olivier Messiaen - Regard du silence (from Vingt regards sur l’enfant-Jésus) Unsuk Chin - Etudes nos. 1, 2 and 6 (In C, Sequences, Grains)
Rolf Hind studied piano and composition at the Royal College of Music in London and in Los Angeles. For fifteen years he worked principally as a pianist, collaborating with composers including Messiaen, Berio, Ligeti, Kurtág, Tan Dun, John Adams, Thomas Adès and George Benjamin, and premiering hundreds of new works worldwide. He returned to composition in 2000, inspired particularly by India, whose languages, philosophy, landscapes and culture inform much of his music. His works include the piano concerto Maya-Sesha, Lost in Thought, a four-hour ‘mindfulness opera’, The Secret Names, and Sky In A Small Cage, his opera about the poet Sufi Rumi.

entry.title: Expanding the Art Song Canon - Introducing Afrikaans Art Song

media:group.media:title: Expanding the Art Song Canon - Introducing Afrikaans Art Song
media:group.media:description:
Stay up to date with the University of Leeds International Concert Series by following us on social media @UoLConcerts - https://linktr.ee/uolconcerts Also sign up to our newsletter - https://bit.ly/361BVoK
---------------------------------------------------
In this recital three South Africans Bronwen Forbay (soprano), Christiaan Bester (baritone), and Nico de Villiers (piano) come together to present a programme of Afrikaans art song. In their seminal work "Afrikaans Art Song Literature: Translation and Pronunciation Guide" (Oxford University Press, 2025), Forbay and Bester introduce the essentials of Afrikaans lyric diction while highlighting the richness, depth, and socio-political context of its art song repertoire for soprano and baritone. Forbay is Associate Professor of Voice at Furman University (Greenville, South Carolina, USA). Bester is Associate Professor of Voice & Director of Opera at Oklahoma State University (Stillwater, Oklahoma, USA). De Villiers is the Deputy Head of Vocal Studies at the Royal Northern College of Music, Manchester.

media:group.media:description:

---------------------------------------------------
Legrand, Weill and the American Songbook
Sam Braysher (alto saxophone) Annie Majin (vocals) Matyas Gayer (piano) Andrew Robb (double bass) Steve Brown (drums)
Sam Braysher, “whose warm tone and consonant and inquisitive approach to harmony is attracting growing attention on the British jazz scene”, (All About Jazz) is a London-based alto saxophonist, who has received widespread critical acclaim for his three albums to date, and for his international collaborations with Sara Dowling, Michael Kanan and Jorge Rossy.
He is joined by a rising star of London’s thriving jazz scene: Annie Majin, fresh from her West End musical theatre debut, whose charming, powerful voice is inspired by Barbara Streisand, Blossom Dearie and the sounds of classic Broadway shows.
Accompanying is an all-star rhythm section, comprising Hungarian pianist Matyas Gayer (Eddie Henderson, Jim Rotondi), award-winning bassist Andrew Robb (Julian Joseph) and ultra swinging drummer Steve Brown (Barry Harris, Scott Hamilton).
Following a string of sold out shows at the likes of Ronnie Scott’s and the London Jazz Festival, Sam’s new album explores the work of beloved French film composer Michel Legrand, the beloved French film composer. Expect to hear inventive interpretations of classics and hidden gems from the Legrand catalogue, in addition to music by adjacent composers including Kurt Weill, Rodgers & Hammerstein and Harold Arlen.

entry.title: Toby Shaer, Archie Moss and Jack Warnock

media:group.media:title: Toby Shaer, Archie Moss and Jack Warnock
media:group.media:description:
Stay up to date with the University of Leeds International Concert Series by following us on social media @UoLConcerts - https://linktr.ee/uolconcerts Also sign up to our newsletter - https://bit.ly/361BVoK
---------------------------------------------------
Toby Shaer, Archie Moss and Jack Warnock are a dynamic trio bringing together English, Irish and European traditional music with fresh arrangements, powerful musicianship and heartfelt song. Expect driving tunes, rich harmony and beautifully delivered vocals — a compelling blend of energy and warmth.
A brand-new trio formed by three seasoned session musicians, this collaboration between Archie Moss, Toby Shaer, and Jack Warnock was born out of a shared love for traditional music from the UK, Ireland, and mainland Europe. Since meeting in 2019, the trio have established themselves not only as dynamic performers but also as sensitive reinterpreters of the tradition.
Each artist is well respected in their own right: Archie Moss (accordion) is a BBC award-winning musician, a celebrated composer, and one of the most in-demand button accordion players in the UK, has performed alongside Seth Lakeman, Sam Sweeney, and Eliza Carthy.
Toby Shaer (fiddle, flute, whistles, cittern) is a multi-instrumentalist, composer, and producer from the southeast of England. Over the past ten years, he has toured extensively across Europe, Australia, and China with revered artists such as Cara Dillon, McCusker, McGoldrick, Doyle, and, alongside Archie Moss, with Sam Kelly & the Lost Boys.
Jack Warnock (guitar, vocals) hails from Co. Derry in Ireland. An award-winning guitarist and singer, he is also an avid Gaeilgeoir (Irish speaker), performing songs in both Irish and English. His compositions and repertoire are steeped in storytelling as he embraces the lineage of folk music in its truest form.
This trio approach their craft and arrangements with delicacy and thought, drawing influence from a plethora of traditions. A collaboration of three like-minded musicians presenting folk music through a contemporary lens.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart - Regina coeli, KV 276 Michael Haydn - O vos omnes Marianna Martines - Miserere mei, Deus Michael Haydn - Tenebrae factae sunt Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart - Ave verum corpus, KV 618 Joseph Haydn - Little Organ Mass
Clothworkers Consort of Leeds performs a programme of Austrian sacred music from the Classical period. The programme includes Mozart’s Regina Coeli K276 for soloists, choir and chamber orchestra and his famous Ave verum corpus along with Joseph Haydn’s Little Organ Mass. The programme also includes a setting of Psalm 50 Miserere mei, Deus by Haydn’s pupil, Marianna Martines, and two motets by his younger brother Michael.
